Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this. Procurement asked us to produce an assurance packet for our internal reviewers outlining how Redwood isolates tenant workloads and how the network/egress model reduces cross-tenant blast radius. Specifically they want:

- A labeled network topology showing control plane vs data plane boundaries, sidecar placement, and egress choke points.
- A short threat-model summary (1 page) highlighting likely attack paths and mitigations for lateral movement and exfiltration.
- Evidence files for operator access controls, KMS/HSM boundaries, and telemetry provenance (logs/traces).

Can you confirm what you can share publicly vs redacted? Also we have a procurement cutoff on Friday 2026-11-05 EOD — can you provide the packet by then?

Appreciate it,
Alex

Hi all — attaching the first-draft topology and an evidence summary. Notes below sketch the key isolation design so Cardinal's reviewers can map controls to attack paths.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_topology_v3.png (image/png)] [Attachment: encapsulation-evidence_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

Topology highlights (short):
- Control plane (managed by Redwood control cluster) is logically separated from tenant inference fabric via VPC-per-customer constructs plus dedicated control-plane endpoints; control-plane traffic is TLS 1.3 mutual auth only.
- Data plane uses per-tenant compute pools with enforced network ACLs at the hyperplane: tenant subnets are hosted in isolated namespace blocks with egress-only endpoints (sidecar egress proxy).
- Sidecar pattern: each inference worker injects a minimal L7 sidecar that performs egress filtering, request provenance tagging, and prefix/KV-cache scoping; sidecars authenticate to a per-tenant service account bound in the control plane.
- KV cache residency: KV caches are sharded per-tenant and stored in encrypted memory or ephemeral SSDs depending on instance class; cross-tenant cache leakage mitigations include allocation fencing and runtime attestation.
- KMS/HSM: customer-encrypted keys are stored in a dedicated HSM cluster (separate tenancy) and referenced via a control-plane proxy which logs key access events to an immutable audit stream.

Evidence included in PDF: RBAC matrix snapshot (redacted), audit-tail sample (last 30 days, redacted), KMS access ledger excerpt, sidecar image hash + SBOM excerpt.

Caveats/assumptions: we cannot share raw operator usernames or production IPs. The topology PNG is safe for procurement review; the evidence PDF contains redacted traces suitable for audit review but not public reproduction.

Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Inline excerpt from topology: "Tenant A compute pools -> tenant-A-egress-proxy -> shared outbound NAT cluster (per-region) -> egress inspection (optional SIEM tap) -> customer-defined egress endpoints"]

Thanks Ben — that level of detail is really helpful. A few follow-ups from our security reviewers: 

1) How do you prove operator session immutability — do you maintain WORM logs or a tamper-evident chain for operator actions?
2) Key rotation cadence and whether customers can rotate keys on-demand (and if rotation requires rolling inference workloads).
3) Any measurable latency overhead when tenant-sidecar enforced egress + per-tenant KV sharding is enabled (we care about 95th pct impact).
4) For the one-page threat lifecycle, could you include a short prioritized list of mitigations we can require contractually?

We need a version of the packet that we can hand to our audit team by Fri 11/05 EOD. If items 1–3 require deeper technical notes, a short appendix is fine. Can you confirm you'll include a one-page threat summary and a checklist of contractual mitigations?

Alex

Alex — great questions. Confirming scope and deliverables:

Deliverables we will provide by Fri 2026-11-05 EOD (final):
- Topology PNG (redwood_topology_v3.png) — labeled control/data plane, sidecar/eBPF placement, egress flow.
- Evidence bundle (encapsulation-evidence_v1.pdf) — RBAC snapshot (redacted), KMS access ledger excerpt, audit-tail sample with tamper-hash markers, SBOM excerpt for sidecar.
- One-page threat lifecycle summary (attached to packet) — prioritized mitigations and recommended contractual clauses (data residency, key rotation SLA, audit access).
- Short appendix answering the three technical follow-ups you raised (operator log immutability, rotation cadence, measured latency impact).

Quick answers to the items you flagged: 
1) Operator session immutability: we ship operator audit events to an append-only ledger signed with a rotation-protected key; ledger entries include operation hash and are stored in a write-once retention bucket for 90 days by default (longer retention is available as an add-on).
2) Key rotation: customers can trigger on-demand key rotation via the control plane API; rotation is orchestrated and does not require full workload restarts for most model architectures — we provide rolling rewraps for active sessions; detailed steps will be in the appendix.
3) Latency: enabling sidecar egress filtering and per-tenant KV sharding adds median token-latency overhead of ~4–8ms and a 95th percentile tail increase of ~12–18ms in our benchmarked workloads (numbers vary by sequence length and instance class); we'll include a measured table from our internal perf runs in the appendix.

Action items (internal): Ben — finalize topology PNG and evidence PDF. Irene — prepare the one-page threat lifecycle and the prioritized contractual mitigations. Karthik — validate ACL wording and provide a short statment for the appendix on subnet ACL defaults.

Alex — we'll post the draft to the Drive link and send a DocuSign-ready checklist if procurement requests any contractual language changes. If you'd like, we can do a 20-minute walk-through with your audit team Thu 11/04 09:00–09:30 PT.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
